title: What are error boundaries and how do you use them?
description: Containing render-time crashes, class-based getDerivedStateFromError, Suspense fallbacks, and what error boundaries cannot catch.

data.text: **Question:** What are error boundaries and how do you use them?

Error boundaries are React components that catch **JavaScript errors during rendering, in lifecycle methods, and in constructors** anywhere in their child tree, display a fallback UI instead of letting the whole app unmount, and log the error. They're implemented as class components with `static getDerivedStateFromError()` (set fallback state) and `componentDidCatch()` (log/report). Placement matters: wrap at feature boundaries (a widget, a route section, the app shell) so one broken page doesn't blank the entire site — but boundaries cannot catch errors in event handlers, async code, `setTimeout`, SSR rendering, or the boundary's own render.

**How they work:**
- During render, an error thrown by a child bubbles to the **nearest** boundary above it (like try/catch, but across the component tree)
- `getDerivedStateFromError(error)` — render-phase; return partial state marking the error (don't side-effect here)
- `componentDidCatch(error, info)` — commit-phase; log `info.componentStack` to your error reporter (Sentry, App Insights)
- Once a boundary catches, the subtree unmounts — its state and effects are gone; the fallback renders instead

**Placement strategy:**
- **Route/feature level**: a crashed dashboard shows an inline 'something went wrong' with a retry, while the nav and other tabs keep working
- **Widget level**: an embedded chart or ad slot failing shouldn't take down the article around it
- **App shell level**: last-resort boundary with a 'reload' button
- Retry: resetting the boundary (key change or state reset) can recover from transient errors — offer 'Try again'
- Errors in a boundary's own render propagate upward to the next boundary — chain them deliberately

**What they DON'T catch (and what to use instead):**
- Event handlers: wrap handler bodies in try/catch and surface state — boundaries don't see clicks
- Async continuations: `await`-thrown errors and promise rejections escape; handle with `.catch` or in error-first patterns
- `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/event callbacks: same — outside React's render pass
- `console.error`-only paths, SSR/client errors (Next.js has its own error.tsx conventions per route)
- Errors during rendering of the boundary itself
- Network/UI errors returned as values (404, empty state) — render normal fallback UI, don't throw for business outcomes

**Modern ecosystem note:** the class requirement stays (no hook equivalent for catching render errors), but libraries wrap it: Next.js `error.tsx`, error boundary wrapper components you can style. React 19 added `onCaughtError`/`onUncaughtError` root handlers for observability.

data.title: A boundary with logging and retry
Boundaries are a seatbelt, not error handling
data.text: An error boundary means a part of your UI failed and the user is seeing a fallback — that's damage control, not a solution. Every catch should report to telemetry with the component stack, and expected failures (network, validation, permissions) should be modeled as states, not thrown as errors. A boundary firing in production is a bug signal, not normal flow.

Interviewers want to assess:
- Knowing it's class-only (no hook catches render errors) and the two-method contract
- Precise list of what it can't catch: events, async, timers
- Placement thinking: blast radius, retry UX, telemetry with component stacks
- Distinction between error states (thrown) and error values (rendered)

items: One boundary at the root only — a widget crash blanks the whole page
Expecting boundaries to catch event-handler or promise errors
Forgetting componentDidCatch telemetry — fallback shown, bug invisible to the team
Not resetting on retry — the same error re-throws immediately
Throwing for business outcomes (404, empty list) instead of rendering states
Swallowing errors with empty fallbacks — user sees blank space and no explanation

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Catch render/lifecycle errors; NOT events, async, or timers
Nest by blast radius: widget → feature → app shell
Always log with component stacks; model expected failures as states
data.takeaway: Place error boundaries like firewalls around features, report every catch to telemetry, and keep thrown errors for genuine faults — everything else is a state you render.
